data.title: As manufacturing labor shortages persist, robots help fill the gap
data.description:
U.S. companies are installing more robots in their factories and warehouses to help offset rising costs and labor shortages.

North American companies ordered 10,989 robots valued at $723.5M in the third quarter, data from the Association for Advancing Automation (A3) showed. That's about 25% more than the year-ago period.

Several industries saw substantial increases in robot orders during Q3, from automotive and semiconductors to life sciences. 

"The broader mix points to a robotics market that is becoming increasingly diversified across industries and applications," said Alex Shikany, executive vice president at A3.

While the automotive sector has been deploying robots at a scale needed to justify their cost for years, technological advances are helping other industries catch up.

Sectors including logistics, agriculture, life sciences and electronics together account for more than half of North American robot orders, A3's Shikany told the Financial Times.

Robot deployment is expected to further ramp up across industries in the years ahead. "Structural demand drivers, including labor shortages, productivity requirements, and manufacturing investment, remain supportive," S&P Global noted.

Labor shortages have been a persistent challenge in the manufacturing sector. A 2024 study from the Manufacturing Institute and Deloitte projected that the U.S. manufacturing industry may need some 3.8M jobs to be filled within the next decade.

With manufacturers struggling to recruit and retain talent, robots can help fill the gap. Industrial robots are effective when it comes to grunt work, but they require costly and extensive programming to handle more complex processes.

"AI could ease these constraints through improved machine vision, automated programming, simulation, and motion planning," S&P stated.

Deploying robots can also be an effective counter to another worrying trend – declining birth rates.

Around 26% of the manufacturing workforce is aged 55 or older. Only 8% are aged 16 to 24, compared to about 13% in other sectors.

All these factors have led to companies accelerating automation, pushing robot density in the global manufacturing sector to a new peak.

Robot density is the number of operational industrial robots relative to the number of employees, as measured by the International Federation of Robotics. The global average baseline has risen to 152 units per 10,000 employees within five years (2020-2025).

South Korea is at the top of leaderboard, with 1,066 industrial units per 10,000 employees. Singapore is in second place with 873 units, while Germany is third, at 469 units.

Meanwhile, the U.S. is ranked 8th worldwide with 323 units per 10,000 employees. The U.S. also trails China in terms of manufacturing and deploying robots.

"We need to double, triple the amount of robotic automation within 5-8 years, or I believe we will lose a significant share of what remains of our manufacturing to China," Robert Atkinson, founder of the Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, told FT. "But we're nowhere near."

Notable robotics firms include Agility Robotics (AGLT), Hyundai (HYMLF)-owned Boston Dynamics, Tesla (TSLA), Figure AI, Apptronik, XPeng (XPEV), Unitree, Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), Symbotic (SYM), Teradyne (TER), Rockwell Automation (ROK), Cognex (CGNX), Serve Robotics (SERV), Ouster (OUST), Knightscope (KSCP) 

AI models and frameworks for robotics include Gemini Robotics and RT-2 from Google (GOOGL), Nvidia's (NVDA) GR00T and Hugging Face's LeRobot.

data.title: Wall Street trades mixed as the Dow rebounds but tech remains under pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were mixed on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year, as fresh weakness in artificial intelligence stocks fueled wider market concerns.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -1.6%. 

From a sector-by-sector basis, eight of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area. 

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's (ANT) much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities. 

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) dropped 9 basis points to 4.67%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) shifted down 8 basis points to 4.96%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) moved down 5 basis points to 5.35%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. (FICO) advanced +6.2%, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) dropped -10.5%.

data.title: Google shifts 2027 AI chip orders from Broadcom to MediaTek, Ming-Chi Kuo says
data.description:
• Google (GOOGL) (GOOG) is cutting planned shipments of its Broadcom-designed (AVGO) AI chips for 2027 while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek, according to analyst Ming-Chi Kuo.
  • Google has reduced its planned shipments of its TPU 8i series by about 1M units, or roughly 20%, Kuo said in a social media post, citing his latest industry survey. 
  • Most of the cuts involve the higher-priced 8i Max, also known as Whalefish, Kuo said.
  • Google plans to increase shipments of its TPU 8t series, which is designed by MediaTek, although the details have not been finalized, Kuo said.
  • "Google has repeatedly stressed in recent months that frontier model development gets first call on compute, and this shift in the 8t and 8i shipment mix is precisely the adjustment it's making amid a tight supply chain and data center power constraints," Kuo said.

data.title: FirstEnergy raises earnings growth guidance, boosts five-year capex plan to $38B
data.description:
FirstEnergy (FE) rose 1.6% in early trading Friday after saying it is raising its long-term adjusted earnings per share compound annual growth rate outlook for 2026-30 to 7%-9%, targeting the upper half of the range, from its prior forecast of 6%-8%, and lifted its five-year capital spending plan.

West Virginia's Public Service Commission issued an order earlier this week granting a certificate to ​two FirstEnergy (FE) subsidiaries to build the Maidsville Energy Center ​combined-cycle gas facility and approved a new generation surcharge ​that allows the companies to recover financing ​costs while the project is under construction.

As a result of the order, the company increased its 2026-30 capital investment plan to $38B from $36B previously and said it plans to fund ~35% of the capex associated with the Maidsville project with equity and/or equity-like securities, raising its total anticipated equity financing needs for the 2026-30 period to $2.8B from $2B.

data.title: Pagaya, Symbotic among industrial stocks to join Russell 3000; Microvast, Energous to exit
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to join or leave the Russell 3000 Index as part of its annual reconstitution.

Following industrial companies are slated to join the index: Pagaya Technologies (PGY), Symbotic (SYM), AerCap Holdings N.V. (AER), DHI Group (DHX), Terrestrial Energy (IMSR).

Industrial firms leaving the index include: Microvast Holdings (MVST), Energous (WATT), Sidus Space (SIDU), RF Industries (RFIL) and Commercial Vehicle Group (CVGI).

The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11.

data.title: Nike takes over as official partner of Formula 1
data.description:
Nike (NKE) is now the new official partner of Formula 1 (FWONK) (FWONA) (FWONB), a partnership that will give the sportswear giant a new promotional outlet and the global racing entity new ways to monetize the Formula 1 brand.

Beginning with the 2027 race season, Nike will outfit racing staff, launch new Formula 1-inspired collections, and create race-weekend experiences to engage fans at the track and beyond.

“Formula 1 is driven by competition, speed, and a constant push to innovate," says Nike CEO Elliott Hill. "That’s an athlete mindset, and it’s one we share at Nike. Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes, and inspire fans around the world.”

The Nike/Formula 1 collaboration will debut on November 20 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix event. The collection will be available at the Nike Las Vegas store at Caesars Palace and the F1 Hub at The Venetian Resort.

Nike (NKE) will also be the official sportswear partner of F1 ACADEMY, the all-female racing series.

Nike’s (NKE) selection ends Puma’s (PMMAF) 3-year official partnership with Formula 1 (FWONK) and brings together two of the largest brands in global sports.

Jefferies’ Anthony Berni views the partnership as especially beneficial to Formula 1 (FWONK) (FWONA) (FWONB). While the financial contribution from Nike is undisclosed, “the deal is directionally supportive of our expectations for continued growth in FWONK sponsorship revenue,” and likely includes an “upsized” partnership from Nike that was not in the deal with Puma.

“Nike’s sponsorship deal reinforces our view that sponsorship remains an attractive source of asset-light growth for Formula 1,” Berni said in a note to clients. 

For Nike (NKE) the benefit is measured in increased brand visibility, crucially in a global sport that draws higher-income spectators. Unfortunately for Nike (NKE) the partnership with Formula 1 does not include Puma’s lucrative and exclusive trackside merchandise-retailing rights and only includes merchandise selling rights at flagship stores and select Formula 1 retail hubs.

data.title: SpaceX's AI-coding platform Cursor considers phasing out use of Chinese models: report
data.description:
Cursor, an AI-powered coding platform acquired by SpaceX (SPCX) in August, is considering phasing out the usage of Chinese AI models in its products, according to a report by the U.S. House Committee on Homeland Security and the House Select Committee on China.

Cursor developed its coding model Composer 2 with Kimi K2.5, an AI model created by the China-based AI lab Moonshot. However, Cursor plans to "explore phasing out PRC (People's Republic of China)-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk," the report said, which was first seen by CNBC. Other U.S. companies, such as Airbnb (ABNB) and DoorDash (DASH), also took part in the committees' investigation on the use of Chinese AI models.

Chinese AI models have experienced widespread adoption by companies around the world, due in part to lower costs while also providing near-frontier model capabilities, the report said. The U.S. also lacks competitive open-weight alternatives at the "price and performance the market demands."

"Beijing is now seeking to turn those technological gains into global market share and long-term dependence," the report added.

The House committees are expected to recommend a national initiative to develop domestic open-weight frontier models for training.

SpaceX shares were down 4% during Friday morning market action.

data.title: Consumer sentiment revised slightly higher in November's final print
data.description:
The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November was revised up to 51.5 from the initial estimate of 51.0, according to data released on Friday. That compared with 48.0 in October.

Current economic conditions: 49.4 vs. the preliminary reading of 51.0 and 46.7 in the prior month.

Consumer expectations: 52.9 vs. 50.9 initial estimate and 48.8 in October.

One-year inflation expectations: +3.7% vs. +4.3% initial estimate and +4.7% in the previous month.

Five-year implied inflation: +3.3% vs. +3.4% preliminary print and +3.5% in October.

 Developing… Check back for updates.

data.title: Musk's control ambitions could drive Tesla-SpaceX merger, HSBC says
data.description:
HSBC has upgraded Tesla (TSLA) to Hold from Reduce, raising its price target to $359 from $157, as speculation over a potential merger with SpaceX (SPCX) reshapes the electric-vehicle maker’s investment narrative.

PT represents a downside of about 4% from the stock's last close.

Analyst Michael Tyndall said the strategic rationale for combining the two companies was not immediately apparent, with limited near-term operational synergies given their different end markets. Instead, they see “control as the key motivation” behind the potential deal, particularly given Elon Musk’s greater voting power at SpaceX (SPCX).

Tyndall believes SpaceX (SPCX) could emerge as the surviving entity, allowing Musk to retain majority voting control in the combined group. Musk owns about 39% of SpaceX (SPCX), carrying 70% of its voting rights, compared with roughly 20% ownership and voting control at Tesla (TSLA).

The analyst estimates a 33% acquisition premium could value Tesla (TSLA) at $507 per share, implying a 50:50 weighted target price of $359 when combined with its fundamental valuation.

A merger could also reduce future equity dilution for SpaceX (SPCX), whose substantial AI and data centre investment requirements exceed Tesla’s (TSLA) capital needs.

However, HSBC flagged regulatory risks, particularly around China, given Tesla’s (TSLA) significant manufacturing and revenue exposure there.

“Bigger could be better,” the analyst said, while maintaining a Hold rating on SpaceX (SPCX) with a $150 price target.

data.description:
